limitations: The preparation is the developing mouse retinogeniculate system. Engulfment is assayed at P5, segregation at P10/P30 and synaptic puncta at P32-35. Adult maintenance, immune surveillance, disease and all brain regions are not established by these developmental endpoints.

TTX/forskolin are intraocular pharmacological manipulations; CTB labeling follows 4-5 h later. Left-eye drug and right-eye vehicle inputs are compared within selected dLGN regions. Relative labeled-input engulfment is not a direct measurement of every synapse firing rate.

CR3/CD11b and C3 knockouts are developmental whole-animal genotypes. Local attribution to microglia is supported by CR3 expression and absence of other CR3-positive cells in the inspected P5 dLGN; the manipulation is not a microglia-restricted inducible knockout.

CTB-positive volume inside reconstructed microglia, projection overlap and juxtaposed VGlut2/GluR1 puncta are distinct anatomical observables. They do not directly measure synaptic efficacy or prove one exclusive sequence of activity, complement tagging and engulfment.

Engulfment is reduced, not abolished, in CR3/C3 knockouts. Complement-independent and nonphagocytic mechanisms remain possible. Raw images, complete supplementary methods and the updated supplementary document remain unread; sex is not established by the selected main methods.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. Figure 1c reports residual responses after an approximately 80% reduction.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.

limitations: Both male and female mice at least seven weeks old were used; exact age and sex distributions per assay group are not supplied. No randomized animal allocation, blinded investigation or prospective statistical sample-size calculation is reported. The reporting summary discusses stimulus ordering separately; it does not establish randomized animal groups.

LPS doses differ across assays: 50 micrograms/kg for FOS and TRAP, 0.5 mg/kg for the main photometry comparison, 0.1 mg/kg for cytokine chemogenetics and 12.5 mg/kg for survival. These exposures are not interchangeable. LPS endotoxaemia is distinct from viable bacterial infection.

Survival experiments use separate Trpa1-cre nodose and Dbh-cre cNST cohorts after high-dose LPS, with repeated 5 mg/kg CNO dosing. Figure 6 shows survival through nine days, not a lifelong or clinical outcome. Separate infection experiments use oral Salmonella and eight CNO injections beginning twelve hours before inoculation; bacterial load is measured in spleen and mesenteric lymph nodes at day five.

Descending efferent routes and immune effector cells remain unresolved. A whole-animal Myd88 knockout does not isolate immune-cell-specific mediation. Lower circulating inflammatory cytokines do not imply universally better defense: sustained TRPA1-population activation increased Salmonella tissue burden in the separate live-infection assay.

Raw measurements, animal identifiers and custom code have not been obtained or replayed. Exclusion criteria include unsuccessful targeting/expression/ablation, but counts and operational thresholds are incomplete. Extended Data 9c reports Gpr65 IL-6 P=0.03 despite a broad no-appreciable-effect conclusion; its small plotted decrease must not be turned into an all-population null. No numerical edge weight or universal carrier count is assigned.
claims.scope: Specified mouse population, intervention, comparator, exposure route and assay window; no universal immune mechanism or clinical efficacy claim.
claims.statement: Neural, endocrine, humoral and vascular routes motivate a broader model of neuroimmune regulation. The reviewed mouse assays do not establish one universal stabilizing process, a depression mechanism, minimal carrier counts or all proposed cross-level dependencies.

limitations: Wild-type C57BL/6J experiments use male mice aged three to four months. The ATP-depletion assay uses mixed microvessel lysates, including endothelial cells, distal pericytes and astrocyte endfeet. Residual ATP is an inverse kinase-activity proxy under added substrate/cofactors, not direct membrane PIP2 concentration. GTPgammaS is not selective for Arf6. Results give 0.012% DMSO whereas Methods give 0.01%; exact solvent concentration needs resolution.

NAV-2729 is pharmacological and not exclusively Arf6-selective. Main Methods describe additional GEF/GAP targets in overlapping concentration ranges. Genetic comparisons and supplementation constrain interpretation but do not identify a unique PIP2-mediated route or exclude effects in other neurovascular cells.

Separate supporting information, animal identifiers, raw recordings and analysis code remain unread or unavailable here. Main Figures 1-4 and Methods support scoped reported outcomes, not independent reproduction of data, exclusions, nesting or statistics. Supplemental genotype, blood-pressure, glucose and lower-dose controls are not independently admitted.

PIP2 availability is inferred from kinase and Kir current assays; the study does not directly quantify membrane lipid abundance or test all Arf6 pathways. Cross-preparation consistency does not prove that this is the sole mediator of blood-flow responses or a universal rule for constructing the graph.

limitations: Cross-sectional postmortem hippocampal samples compare young adults (YA), healthy agers (HA), preclinical intermediate pathology (PCI), Alzheimer disease (AD) and SuperAgers (SA). There is no randomized diagnosis, in vivo birthdating, lineage follow-up, electrophysiology or neurogenesis intervention.

The main text reports 38 participants, including eight HA, whereas both cohort-table sheets and the abundance workbook contain 39 sample IDs, including nine HA. Identical demographic/pathology fields occur for some different IDs; this does not prove duplicate donors. The donor/sample manifest and independence remain unresolved.

Rare cell labels depend on quality filtering, reference-assisted annotation, marker expression and model-based trajectory inference. RNA-velocity latent time is not elapsed lineage time. A UMAP embedding is not measured physical tissue geometry.

The abundance analysis uses per-sample counts and library-size normalization, not absolute whole-hippocampus numbers or neuron birth rates. Published log-fold changes and adjusted P values are retained as reported comparisons; edgeR analysis and sequencing data have not been rerun.

SuperAgers come from Northwestern, while the other groups come from the University of Washington. Tissue source, individual variability and clinical selection can confound group comparisons. The Methods and main text differ in their reference age wording for SuperAger memory criteria; a uniform clinical manifest is required.

Reviewed material comprises main pages 1264-1267, Discussion on page 1272, Methods covering donors, nuclei isolation, sequencing and admitted analyses, Figure 2, Extended Data Figures 1 and 4 and all three reporting-summary pages. Main pages 1268-1271 and the remaining extended-data analyses were not fully reviewed.

Original Supplementary Tables 1 and 8 and the table legends were read; selected numeric cells and the complete sample/count census are checked locally. Other supplementary table contents were not audited. GEO GSE268609 is named by the paper, but its sample manifest and raw data were not obtained; no study-specific executable code was replayed.

The SA immature-cell comparison is significant against HA and AD, but not against YA or PCI at the table adjusted-P threshold of 0.05. These distinct contrasts neither prove no difference nor establish that generating neurons preserves memory.

The study measures morphology and output transmission, not behavior. Proposed recruitment of existing spines is a cross-sectional interpretation, not an observed minimal construction rule or proof of memory necessity.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

Main Figure 2c alternates the order of contexts across days, whereas the discrimination Methods describe training context A followed one hour later by similar context B. The exact per-animal schedule requires reconciliation. The nine-day ratio analysis reports treatment P=0.023; its day F/degree-of-freedom/P combination also needs correction. Handling of a zero sum of freezing scores is unspecified.

Contextual freezing discrimination is a behavioral proxy for pattern separation, not a direct measurement of DG neural population codes or general memory improvement. Supplementary protocol variants have treatment P=0.38 and P=0.06 despite interactions or day-specific differences; they cannot be pooled as uniformly positive main effects.

Supplementary Figure 14 reports an overall discrimination-ratio treatment P=0.1 and interaction P=0.3. Late within-group differences are not a between-group necessity test. Its day-five F(1,14)=4.34/P=0.04 pair needs reconciliation; no replacement biological P value is calculated here.

The paper explicitly leaves functional significance untested. No electrical recording, identified synaptic output, behavioral mediation or selective birth-cell perturbation establishes functional integration in these human samples. Findings in mouse integration experiments cannot supply those missing human measurements.

Whole hippocampi were analyzed; the investigators could not separately radiocarbon-date hippocampal subdivisions. Dentate localization and absolute cell-number scaling rely on other histological and stereological studies. The approximately 700 neurons per day in each hippocampus and 0.004% of dentate neurons per day are model-dependent estimates, not directly counted daily births.

No human electrical, identified synaptic-output or selective behavioral assay is performed. Similar estimated rates across species do not supply human functional integration or a birth-to-cognition mechanism. Histology, isotope dating, molecular markers and rodent interventions remain distinct evidence.

No electrical, synaptic-output, learning or memory assay was performed. A possible cognitive role, stable-memory benefit or recovery mechanism remains untested. Labeling in this study does not require an injury or learning manipulation and does not validate the source card's necessary incoming assertions, weights or minimum carrier counts.

Specific rat learning protocols alter retained birth labels; a separate macaque study supplies age-limited neuronal colabels. Neither establishes a universal learning prerequisite or a selective newborn-neuron requirement for memory.

Rakic (1985) and Eckenhoff and Rakic (1988) propose that stable neurons preserve learned information. Their autoradiographic nulls contain no matched memory test and appear to share specimens. This proposed stability mechanism and later renewal-benefit hypotheses are not adjudicated by histology alone.

Pattern separation, temporal context and memory resolution remain nonexclusive interpretations. Behavioral discrimination, population-code decorrelation and temporal association require different measurements; review schematics cannot choose among them.
claims.scope: The stated species, labeling method, preparation and observable. No universal level transition, numerical edge weight or physical instance is admitted.
claims.statement: A complete neuron-birth-to-memory route remains a hypothesis. Mouse physiology and a Nestin-lineage Bax intervention constrain parts of the route; macaque histology has no matched functional assay. Rat training changes retained birth labels without isolating survival or testing newborn-cell necessity. These findings do not establish general cognitive necessity, unique neuron-count mediation or a causal human memory-preservation mechanism. Earlier autoradiographic nulls likewise do not establish that stable neuron populations are necessary for memory.

limitations: NCff mice carry Nestin-CreERT2 and two floxed Bax alleles on a mixed C57BL/6-129/SvEv background. The primary contrast is tamoxifen versus vehicle within NCff, starting at at least eight weeks. Reporter NCY versus NCffY comparisons use separate littermate groups both receiving tamoxifen; Cre-negative Bax-floxed controls are another comparison.

The manipulation reduces Bax-dependent cell death in the Nestin stem/progenitor lineage; it is not a selective increase in birth rate or a dentate-newborn-neuron-only intervention. Olfactory-bulb survival also changes. Reporter recombination is a proxy, and altered cell properties or other lineage effects remain alternative mediators.

citations.note: Preparation, scoring and statistical boundaries apply to this finding.

limitations: Adult male C57BL6 YFP-H mice were approximately 2.5-7 months old. Layer 5 neuronal apical tufts were sampled within the superficial 100 micrometers, typically 100-500 micrometers from the posterior-medial infarct edge; this is selected surviving cortex, not the whole injured brain.

Main scientific text, Materials and Methods, and Figures 1-5 with captions are reviewed. Supplemental Figures 1-2 were not obtained or read. Animal-identified image stacks, custom IgorPro routines and the allocation/exclusion manifest were not obtained; no imaging or biological experiment was independently reproduced.

Photothrombosis used Rose Bengal 100 milligrams per kilogram intraperitoneally and 532-nanometer illumination, 17 milliwatts for fifteen minutes, under ketamine-xylazine. Sham controls omitted either dye or illumination. Per-assay sham composition, random allocation and group-specific age distributions are not supplied in the reviewed account.

Imaging under urethane was acute: hourly stacks over six, occasionally seven hours, after a one-, two- or six-week recovery interval, followed by terminal histology. Separate cohorts do not trace the same spine or dendritic arbor continuously from before injury through six weeks.

Only laterally projecting spines were scored. New spines had to protrude at least four pixels, approximately 0.55 micrometers, and remain present at the six-hour endpoint. Transient events, filopodium conversions, shifted segments and poor-quality images were excluded. The assay is not a census of all spine births, losses or synapses.

Turnover is reported as a percentage of the counted spine population over the imaging session; raw animal-level numerator/denominator assignments are unavailable. Spine density is a count per ten micrometers of dendrite. Neither measure is a neuron birth rate, a universal hourly turnover constant or a calibrated graph weight.

Turnover scoring was blinded to experimental condition, but movement, abnormal breathing and image deterioration could exclude experiments; exclusion counts and animal identifiers are not supplied. Axial optical resolution was about 5.3 micrometers, much poorer than lateral resolution, and six spine-appearance cases were pooled across animals for shaft-fluorescence controls.

Spine morphology and adjacent sensory-evoked reflectance do not measure the functional efficacy of each new synapse, selective memory content or behavioral recovery. The Discussion explicitly leaves the causal link between increased formation and recovered function unestablished.

The main text gives a 0.14 percent control formation mean and 1.37, 0.93 and 0.75 percent poststroke means. The abstract describes a five- to eight-fold peak increase; these rounded quantities do not define one exact fold estimate. Retain the reported assay means without calibrating a universal multiplier.

Nonsignificant outcomes are not equivalence or full recovery. Photothrombosis does not permit controlled reperfusion, and the paper does not directly establish the same time course in other stroke models, traumatic injury or humans.

The increase concerns retained new lateral protrusions in the sampled peri-infarct cortex, not continuous weeks-long tracking or neuronal birth.

Global neuronal 2POP fitting reports a renewing fraction near 0.35, with a reported 95% interval of 0.12-0.63. For nonneuronal cells the main text reports 0.51 with interval 0.22-0.88, accepted Table S2 gives 0.56, and individual fits fix 0.55. These summaries must not be treated as one exactly reproduced estimate.

The reported individual medians, 1.75% per year for neurons and 3.5% for nonneuronal cells, apply within fixed renewing fractions of 0.35 and 0.55 after the stated exclusions. Global-fit rates of about 12% and 4.9% per year in Tables S3 and S2 are different estimands. Unfittable samples were excluded from the individual 2POP analysis; Figure 2C/5A additionally states plot limits below 0.001 or above 1.5.

The accepted supplement distinguishes unpaired 2POP comparison (51 neuronal and 64 nonneuronal fractions, rank-sum P=0.005) from 40 matched pairs (signed-rank P=0.054; neuronal median 1.5%, nonneuronal 3.5% per year). The latter null does not establish equal rates. Comparing these tests without their populations and denominators would be misleading.

Age associations use cross-sectional, model-derived rates: reported neuronal r=-0.31, P=0.03 and nonneuronal r=-0.35, P=0.04. They do not trace the same people over time or identify an age intervention. The sex comparison P=0.41 does not establish equivalence. The DCX overlay uses an external Knoth cohort, not birthdating of the same cells.

The accepted supplement prints a heuristic labeled AIC, p + log2(SSE), and requires a halving of SSE per added parameter. Applying that printed rule to rounded Table S2 gives 0.31 > 0.51/2, so its nonneuronal 2POP preference does not follow from that rule. Table S3 has 0.17 < 0.49/2 for neurons. This arithmetic checks reporting consistency only; final supplementary methods, likelihood and code remain unverified.

The source says subjects born around 1955-1965 discriminate 2POP from homogeneous age-dependent alternatives; without them the scenarios could not be distinguished. MCMC explores bounded parameter sets, and fitting several scenarios does not prove a unique biological mechanism. Full numerical replay and out-of-sample discrimination have not been performed.

The fitting procedure assumes a one-year food lag and development beginning six months before birth. Its weighted SSE squares weights of 1 or 2 assigned around a 10-microgram carbon boundary. Table S1 has both estimated DNA carbon mass and reactor-measured mass, including ND entries. The exact mass choice, boundary treatment and missing-value policy require executable code before reproducing the fit.

The supplement explicitly does not explore population feedback: birth and death rates do not depend on the population state. Constant population size in replacement scenarios is imposed by their birth boundary, not observed emergence of a stabilizing rule. Population turnover does not identify one-for-one functional replacement, circuit topology or a universal minimal assembly.

limitations: Eleven animals comprise nine Macaca fascicularis and two M. mulatta, aged 5-23 years. Table 1 provides sex, age, injection number and survival per animal, but site, assay-specific sampling and raw counts are unavailable. All three 23-year-old animals are male M. fascicularis.

BrdUrd was 75 mg/kg intraperitoneally, one to five injections separated by 24 hours. Five single-injection animals survived two hours; six animals with three or five injections survived one or two weeks after the last injection. One Results paragraph instead says after the first injection. This timing conflict remains unresolved.

Methods explicitly states that two hours permits S-phase labeling but not completed mitosis or migration. All three 23-year-old animals have only this two-hour interval. The reported oldest-age BrdU and TOAD-64 profiles do not establish birthdated neuronal differentiation at that age.

The modified optical fractionator uses coded slides and every twelfth 40-micrometre section, excluding the outermost focal plane. Estimates are not raw cell counts or instantaneous birth rates. Table 1 gives dentate BrdUrd estimates of 4308, 3288, 1968, 2748, 1896, 1176, 780, 876, 420, 336 and 228 for animals 1-11. Mixed species, dose accumulation, age and survival prevent a pooled age-specific production rate. limitations: Adult male Sprague Dawley rats weighed 300-350 g; chronological age is not stated. Group sizes are generally five or six. The paper does not provide a complete animal manifest or randomized assignment procedure. Coded histology is reported, not complete blinding of every procedure.

BrdU was 200 mg/kg; the injection route is not specified. In the main experiments labeling occurred one week before four consecutive training days, with separate terminal cohorts 24 hours or seven days after training. The approximate three-week label-age wording does not exactly specify elapsed days. Separate sacrificed cohorts do not track individual cells longitudinally.

Trace conditioning used 200 trials per day for four days, an 83-dB 250-ms noise, a 500-ms gap and a 100-ms 0.7-mA shock. Unpaired rats received the same stimulus counts without explicit pairing. All paired animals reached 60% conditioned responses; none of the unpaired animals did. Complete naive-group electrode and handling matching is not specified.

Delay conditioning uses a 320-ms noise coterminating with an 80-ms shock and a different conditioned-response window. Trace and delay differ in stimulus durations and scoring as well as temporal gap. The reported F(1,19)=4.24, P=0.05 is called nonsignificant; this boundary result and final-day similarity are not statistical equivalence.

Hippocampal dependence is imported from prior lesion literature and, for the exact rat trace protocol, unpublished lesion data. No matched hippocampal lesion or selective newborn-cell manipulation is performed in this histology study. The graph links the specified task protocol to its measured outcome, not generic hippocampal necessity.

limitations: Twelve rhesus monkeys were labeled at reported ages of six months to eleven years; Table 1 gives ages at death of seven months to seventeen years. This is a mixed developmental and adult sample, not twelve animals labeled after puberty. Age at death cannot substitute for age at injection.

One to seven injections of tritiated thymidine were given at 10 mCi/kg. This is radioactivity per body mass, not the later BrdU mass dose. The injection route is not stated. The narrative survival range is three days to more than six years; the table includes 6.3 years. Repeated exposures and long retention windows are not independent animals or instantaneous birth rates.

Heavy labeling was calibrated separately in each case from glial, endothelial or peripheral cells, usually more than 15-30 silver grains per nucleus. Light-microscopic autoradiography exposure was 12-18 weeks and electron-microscopic exposure exceeded 24 weeks. A common fixed threshold cannot be imposed retrospectively. Occasional neuronal profiles with fewer than five or six grains were not classified as newborn; artifact or DNA repair was proposed without a repair assay.

Nine animals were pregnant at injection; neuronal labeling in offspring served as a positive control. Peripheral renewing tissues were also examined. The offspring and tissue checks demonstrate label incorporation under their conditions; they do not establish complete sensitivity for rare adult neuronal births. Pregnancy and assay allocation by animal are unavailable.

Figure 1D-E and Figure 2 use a seven-month-old animal, with Figure 2 explicitly labeled at six months. These images are juvenile examples. Oligodendroglial labels were mostly reported at six and eighteen months, with only occasional postpubertal examples. Selected dentate GFAP and ultrastructural analysis is described without a complete case-by-assay manifest or independent neuronal-marker panel.

limitations: The fit uses selected sequences and group error profiles, with fixed capacity Kmax=12 and chosen noise assumptions. Fitted probabilities combine within-person nonuse and between-person variation; they are not measured fractions of people lacking a resource. No held-out task or neural carrier test is reported.

The printed implementation is not unambiguous: S1 Text gives three repetitions of a two-output program an eight-output example; with binary logarithms its listed Repeat+1 program costs 7 while the figure labels K=5. Main-text 2points/4points costs are 6/9, whereas S1 Figure 2 labels 7/11. The formula, initial-state convention and program inventory require reconciliation before exact minima are admitted.

The reduced-resource description sets disallowed program costs to 12 while the stated threshold admits costs at most 12. Prefix correction, random-choice indexing and selection among programs versus sequences also require reconciliation. Published plots alone do not resolve these choices.

The 2021 MEG supplement repeats the cost-5 repeat description and lists an initial output followed by four pairs for alternate and two-crosses sequences. These descriptions require consistent output-length and cost conventions before executable or minimum-program claims.

Wang et al. (2019) uses alternating two-step and opposing one-step rotations, while Al Roumi et al. (2021) uses three-step and opposing one-step rotations under the same alternate name. Two-crosses is treated as three-level in 2019 and non-nested in the 2021 table. Template identity and parse must be explicit; names do not determine a shared structure.

limitations: The abstract's four macrocomponents and the body's three grouped components are different groupings of the proposed architecture. Pages 82 and 86 describe dissociations between executive-task and theory-of-mind impairments; these secondary summaries require primary review before any specific lesion effect is admitted. They do not calibrate a universal maintenance dependency.

Page 91 states that the proposed psychological constructs are not primitive and still need decomposition. There is no fixed cardinality, measured carrier threshold or numerical weighting of perception, affect and control. Frontal activation can reflect inhibition or monitoring/manipulation of internally generated information; neither is uniquely established by the review.

Roundhouse-dump normalization and a second, energy-sensitive monitor reduce sensitivity to the loaded spectrum; they do not make its distribution identical to the stored population. Short-hold data fit spectral and rolling normalization corrections.

Coincidences begin with two PMTs within 100 ns, extend until a gap above 1000 ns and use a 20 ns fixed dead time; the standard threshold is ten photons. Detector-live-time and photon-tail/pileup corrections are fitted or simulated, not independently replayed here.

Timing was blinded with factors 0.99986-1.00171, but wrongly rejected 2020 runs were restored after unblinding; the reported change to the 2020-2022 combination is about -0.14 s. Final selection must not be described as entirely blinded.

Equation 2 uses an empirically scaled yield-error model with DQE factors, including a net-count rather than independent peak-plus-background variance term. DQE parameters are adjusted from short-hold fluctuations and fit quality; reduced chi-square one is partly imposed, not an independent validation of the noise model.

Rolling normalization uses short holds in overlapping blocks, typically fifteen runs within epochs. Its covariance and uncertainty are not independently reconstructed by dividing a printed yield error by the fitted correction factor.

limitations: The component split has a convention ambiguity of order alpha*(m_d-m_u). The selected convention sets the electromagnetic Sigma-minus/Sigma-plus splitting to zero; the zero is a definition within the stated accuracy, not a measured null result.

Opposite QCD and QED components describe parameter-dependent contributions to mass differences. They are not separately observed forces, measured shares of the nucleon mass or statistical probabilities.

The tabulated total and component values are separately rounded and correlated. For example 2.52-1.00=1.52 MeV from rounded entries does not justify replacing the reported total 1.51 MeV; marginal errors must not be combined as independent components.
About 500 fit variants vary normalization, mass dependence, cutoff terms, two correlator starts and two charge-renormalization scales. They reuse simulation data and are not independent replications.

AIC weights are proportional to exp[-(chi^2+2*p)/2]. The weighted mean gives the central estimate, variation among fits estimates systematic uncertainty, and the complete procedure is repeated on 2000 bootstrap samples for statistical uncertainty. AIC weights are not probabilities of physical truth or graph-edge strengths.

The chosen family includes g^2*a or a^2 discretization terms, mass extrapolations, and a fitted 1/L^3 electromagnetic term after the leading finite-volume corrections. Its uncertainty does not exhaust arbitrary omitted models or higher orders.
The primary Coleman-Glashow combination is fitted rather than constrained to zero. One auxiliary cross-check assumes that relation; it cannot independently verify the relation it imposes.

Three auxiliary analyses reuse the data; details are not fully supplied. One masks mass differences by a random factor between 0.7 and 1.3. This is not independent simulation replication or evidence that every analysis was blinded.

The neutron-proton total is reported as about five standard deviations above zero under the selected error construction. The paper does not supply an independently reproduced discovery p-value here. Comparisons with known masses are postdictions; the 2015 statement that some channels were unmeasured is not a current experimental census.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

Stability in this calculation concerns the included strong and electromagnetic interactions. Weak decays, a neutron lifetime, proton-decay bounds, nuclear stability and real-time hadron formation are outside its calculated scope.

Quark flavors, field components, sources per configuration and fitted states are different counting domains. The calculation establishes no universal constituent minimum or graph-level generative rule.

limitations: These four runs are a subset of the 14 charged production ensembles, not an independent replication of the 41-ensemble result. The temporal extent changes with the spatial box and the QED_L large-time assumptions remain applicable.

The bare coupling e=1.00 is larger than the physical coupling. Figure 1 uses the approximate label bare alpha about 1/10; e^2/(4*pi), the renormalized flow coupling and physical alpha are distinct quantities.
The plotted kaon mass-squared difference is negative at this enhanced coupling. That sign is not the physical kaon mass ordering and is not evidence of a neutron-proton sign reversal.

No significant neutral-kaon volume dependence is resolved in this scan; that does not prove exactly zero corrections. The charged-neutral difference needs a fitted 1/L^3 term in addition to the universal leading terms.

These are reported computational results for the specified action, ensembles and fitting procedure. The 60 TB archive, correlators, covariance matrices and analysis code have not been independently replayed.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

limitations: At the stated precision the recoil prescription is E_B approximately E_gamma + E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2), so the energy-equivalent wavelength is shorter than the photon wavelength. It is not a second detected photon.

The recoil mass is the deuteron nuclear mass, not a deuterium atomic mass or the Kapton molecular mass. Thermal capture and the stated prompt-emission conditions limit this approximation; it is not an exact arbitrary-kinematics formula.

The paper reports a 5e-10 relative uncertainty contribution from recoil constants, negligible at its measurement precision. This does not make recoil itself negligible or set omitted kinematic effects identically to zero.

A capture photon, a binding-energy inference and an inferred neutron mass are different observables. None establishes a free-neutron lifetime, proton stability, a universal constituent minimum or a real-time hadron formation mechanism.

limitations: The adopted atomic relative-mass difference Ar(2H)-Ar(1H)=1.00627674630(71) comes from DiFilippo et al. (1994), cited by Kessler. The primary mass-spectrometry article is reviewed; its unprinted fit covariance and original measurements remain unreproduced.

The paper uses the atomic mass difference plus the mass-equivalent binding energy at its precision. This is not a general exact identification of atomic and nuclear masses; electron binding and charge-state corrections require their own treatment at higher precision.

The published neutron mass is inferred by adding the adopted hydrogen-isotope mass difference and the capture-derived binding-energy mass equivalent. It is not a direct Penning-trap measurement of a neutral neutron.

The quoted uncertainty contributions are 0.42e-9 u from binding energy and 0.71e-9 u from mass spectrometry, with total 0.82e-9 u after rounding. No upstream covariance or raw mass-spectrometry fit is reproduced.

limitations: The five configuration groups are combined as two campaign sets because settings within a campaign share an angle calibration. They are not five independent mass experiments.

The approximately 6 g Kapton source in three graphite holders is exposed to about 5e14 neutrons per square centimeter per second. Its roughly 450 C environment and about 1.2 percent daily hydrogen loss do not describe isolated stationary free neutrons.

Four optical-polygon calibrations near the campaigns use the sum of 24 exterior angles, 2*pi. One serves 1995 and three serve March 1998; the 1998 humidity dependence is about 0.5e-6 per ten percentage points, with calibration relative uncertainty expanded to 1e-7.

limitations: At the stated precision the recoil prescription is E_B approximately E_gamma + E_gamma^2/(2*m_d*c^2), so the energy-equivalent wavelength is shorter than the photon wavelength. It is not a second detected photon.

The recoil mass is the deuteron nuclear mass, not a deuterium atomic mass or the Kapton molecular mass. Thermal capture and the stated prompt-emission conditions limit this approximation; it is not an exact arbitrary-kinematics formula.

The paper reports a 5e-10 relative uncertainty contribution from recoil constants, negligible at its measurement precision. This does not make recoil itself negligible or set omitted kinematic effects identically to zero.

The 1999 inverse-meter conversions are 1.331025045(11)e-15 u and 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. The first is a mass-equivalent conversion h/(m_u*c), the second is hc/e; energy and mass units are not interchangeable without c^2.

The conversions depend on the paper's electron relative mass, fine-structure constant, Rydberg constant and other adopted constants. Their uncertainties are different; changing to modern SI constants is a new calculation, not a silent correction of the published result.

limitations: The 1994 result is a global least-squares solution of twenty pairwise comparisons. Its covariance matrix determines uncertainties of correlated atomic masses and mass differences; the short article does not provide that matrix or every input ratio.
For a mass difference, Var(D-H)=Var(D)+Var(H)-2*Cov(D,H). Adding printed marginal errors in quadrature assumes zero covariance and is not a reconstruction of the published fit.

The authors report reduced chi-square 0.74 and redundant routes to the mass table. These internal checks constrain the stated error model; they do not logically exclude every possible common systematic.

The quoted 2.6e-10 relative rms magnetic fluctuation applies to a single frequency measurement in the 1994 analysis. A typical one-night ratio error near 1e-10 and the final fitted mass uncertainties have different averaging domains.

The 1993 treatment describes approximately Gaussian residuals for its example; the 1994 robust estimator downweights non-Gaussian outliers. These are different analysis descriptions, not interchangeable procedures.
The carbon-12 neutral-atom reference has mass exactly 12 u by definition. A carbon ion differs by electron mass and ionization energy; treating C+ as exactly 12 u is incorrect.

Converting molecular-ion comparisons to neutral isolated ground-state atoms requires electron, chemical-binding and ionization-energy terms. The 1994 analysis uses ideal-gas heats of formation at 0 K; this is not the trap temperature.
A neutral hydrogen atom is not a bare proton and a neutral deuterium atom is not a deuteron. Nuclear masses require removal of electronic contributions.
Table II(b) of the 1993 paper expresses masses in nu (1e-9 u). Its H and D values become 1.0078250317(7) u and 2.0141017779(6) u; the 1994 H value is 1.0078250316(5) u.

Subtracting the printed 1994 D and H central values gives 1.0062767463 u. Kessler adopts the dimensionless relative-mass difference 1.00627674630(71); its 0.71e-9 uncertainty is not independently recovered from the missing mass-fit covariance.

The 1994 neutron value 1.0086649235(23) u already uses the Greene1986 deuteron binding energy. The 1993 neutron value uses the Wapstra1990 binding-energy compilation. Neither is a direct measurement of a neutral neutron in the trap.

The upstream H/D mass information is an input to the capture-based neutron inference. Feeding a neutron mass already derived from capture binding energy back as an independent confirmation would conceal a shared input.
The 1993/1994 mass inputs are historical values. They are not current recommended constants, a new SI kilogram definition or independently traced inputs to the Borsanyi calculation.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

A charged-ion frequency, neutral-atom mass and inferred neutron mass are different quantities. These results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal constituent minimum.

The 1993 and 1994 publications belong to the same MIT measurement program. Disjoint acquisition and cross-publication covariance are not established; the two papers cannot be treated as independent replications or averaged as independent results.

limitations: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

The SOF signal is a classical cyclotron amplitude produced by two separated pulses, not a quantum-state amplitude or an entanglement measurement. Figure 1 uses evolution times up to 50 s for the precision estimate.

Figure 2 compares an N+ ion at approximately 5 V with the same species at 10 V and an N2+ ion at 10 V, with a 22.5 mV axial offset. The approximately 3 ppb unequal-voltage shift disappears at the reported precision with the common-voltage procedure.

Table I bounds residual magnetic, electrostatic and relativistic systematic terms at approximately 0.030, 0.025 and 0.020 ppb for the specified N+/N2+ settings. These are configuration-specific error estimates, not zero corrections or universal bounds.

The first two Table II(a) reference ratios depend on electron mass and binding energies. Their agreement near 0.15 ppb tests those controls; it does not prove absence of every systematic effect in all other ion comparisons.
The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

For the same magnetic field, omega_2/omega_1=(m_1/abs(q_1))/(m_2/abs(q_2)). Equal charges permit a mass ratio; the Ar+/Ar++ entry requires the charge factor and is not a literal ratio of almost equal ionic masses.
The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

A charged-ion frequency, neutral-atom mass and inferred neutron mass are different quantities. These results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal constituent minimum.

The 1993 and 1994 publications belong to the same MIT measurement program. Disjoint acquisition and cross-publication covariance are not established; the two papers cannot be treated as independent replications or averaged as independent results.

limitations: Subtracting the printed 1994 D and H central values gives 1.0062767463 u. Kessler adopts the dimensionless relative-mass difference 1.00627674630(71); its 0.71e-9 uncertainty is not independently recovered from the missing mass-fit covariance.

The 1994 neutron value 1.0086649235(23) u already uses the Greene1986 deuteron binding energy. The 1993 neutron value uses the Wapstra1990 binding-energy compilation. Neither is a direct measurement of a neutral neutron in the trap.

The upstream H/D mass information is an input to the capture-based neutron inference. Feeding a neutron mass already derived from capture binding energy back as an independent confirmation would conceal a shared input.
The 1993/1994 mass inputs are historical values. They are not current recommended constants, a new SI kilogram definition or independently traced inputs to the Borsanyi calculation.

The 1994 result is a global least-squares solution of twenty pairwise comparisons. Its covariance matrix determines uncertainties of correlated atomic masses and mass differences; the short article does not provide that matrix or every input ratio.
For a mass difference, Var(D-H)=Var(D)+Var(H)-2*Cov(D,H). Adding printed marginal errors in quadrature assumes zero covariance and is not a reconstruction of the published fit.

The authors report reduced chi-square 0.74 and redundant routes to the mass table. These internal checks constrain the stated error model; they do not logically exclude every possible common systematic.
The carbon-12 neutral-atom reference has mass exactly 12 u by definition. A carbon ion differs by electron mass and ionization energy; treating C+ as exactly 12 u is incorrect.

Converting molecular-ion comparisons to neutral isolated ground-state atoms requires electron, chemical-binding and ionization-energy terms. The 1994 analysis uses ideal-gas heats of formation at 0 K; this is not the trap temperature.
A neutral hydrogen atom is not a bare proton and a neutral deuterium atom is not a deuteron. Nuclear masses require removal of electronic contributions.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

A charged-ion frequency, neutral-atom mass and inferred neutron mass are different quantities. These results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal constituent minimum.

The 1993 and 1994 publications belong to the same MIT measurement program. Disjoint acquisition and cross-publication covariance are not established; the two papers cannot be treated as independent replications or averaged as independent results.

limitations: Neutral carbon-12 has mass exactly 12 u; C-12(6+) instead has mass 12 u minus six electron masses plus the six positive ionization energies divided by c^2. The sixfold charge factor in m_p=R*m_C/6 cannot be omitted.

Heiße 2019 uses m_e=0.000548579909069(15) u and historical electronic-energy inputs. The electron mass is inferred using a bound-electron g factor and QED; it is not an independently reproduced direct weighing in this review.

Heiße 2017 prints m_C=11.9967096264139(10) u and 0.08 ppt relative uncertainty. Heiße 2019 prints 11.99670962641385(8) u but still states 0.08 ppt; the printed (8) corresponds to about 0.00667 ppt. This unresolved uncertainty discrepancy is not silently repaired.

The proton-electron ratio in Heiße 2019 assumes zero covariance because the dominant proton and electron systematic uncertainties differ. That assumption is not proof of complete statistical independence.

The stored ions are measured alternately under the same trap voltages, using separate axial resonators. Randomized species order reduces linear drift; it does not make sequential measurements simultaneous or statistically independent.
The proton dataset comprises thirteen runs and three ion pairs, with about 300 hours of acquisition over two months. Runs, cycles, ion pairs and publications are not independent replications.
The planar fit extrapolates the deliberately excited cyclotron motion to zero using R_i=R_stat+a*S_p^2+b*S_C^2. Thermal axial and cyclotron motion still requires systematic corrections.
The 2019 reanalysis corrects the estimated ion temperatures and a minor measurement-program flaw in the 2017 datasets. The two publications cannot be averaged as independent proton-mass experiments.

The 2017 abbreviation MT denotes the measurement trap; in 2019 PT denotes the precision trap and MT the magnetometer trap. The proposed simultaneous three-ion readout and magnetic shim coils were not used in the reported proton campaign.

The proton campaign had C4=(0 +/- 6.3)e-6 and C6=(-6.8 +/- 0.4)e-4. The improved Table VI tuning and proposed millikelvin cooling describe other conditions, not the acquisition used for the reported mass.

limitations: COMSOL 5.2 with the AC/DC module represents a point charge and perfectly conducting grounded electrode surfaces. Twenty-one ion positions from -0.5 to +0.5 mm are fitted with odd polynomials to extract field gradients.

Agreement between finite-element and semianalytical calculations is tested on the same simplified geometry. Full electrode geometry changes the LIONTRAP correction by 2.7(4) percent; horizontal and azimuthal slit effects are separately reported.

Numerical/fit and geometry uncertainties have different meanings. The geometry estimate assumes manufacturing deviations up to 10 micrometers; higher-order effects are treated as small under a displacement assumption below 50 micrometers.

The cylinder reference, polynomial order and matrix-truncation checks constrain numerical error. Increasing resolution or expansion order alone does not prove convergence or exact reproduction of the manufactured trap.

The calculation and experiment have shared geometry and calibration assumptions. Their agreement is conditional evidence for an image-charge correction in the stated trap, not a universal graph-generation rule or an independent mass measurement.

For ion charge n*e, Schuh 2019 defines radial actual-minus-ideal shifts Delta_nu_plus/minus=opposite-sign n*E_rho/(2*pi*B0). The correction added to the measured cyclotron estimate is +n*(2*E_rho+E_z)/(4*pi*B0), in Hz. The change of sign convention is explicit in footnote 2.

The infinitely long cylindrical-electrode approximation gives a relative cyclotron correction approximately m/(4*pi*epsilon0*B0^2*rho0^3). Real gaps, electrode shape, displacements and axial fields require a scoped geometry calculation.

The invariance-based cyclotron estimate retains an image-charge correction. Cancellation of the opposite radial shifts in nu_plus+nu_minus does not establish that the squared-frequency reconstruction is unshifted.

limitations: The 2020 reference uses CODATA 2018 m_e=0.000548579909065(16) u, C-12(6+)=11.99670962641246(35) u and C-12(4+)=11.99780583927483(34) u. These differ from the 2019 reference. Neutral carbon-12 is exactly 12 u, but its ions are not.
For the deuteron R=nu_c(C6+)/nu_c(d), m_d=R*m_C6/6; for HD+, R=nu_c(C4+)/nu_c(HD+), m_HD=R*m_C4/4. Charge factors and positive electronic ionization energies cannot be omitted.
The HD+/C4+ acquisition uses one pair over seven weeks and different trapping voltages to match axial frequencies. It is not the common-voltage deuteron preparation.

The HD+ rovibrational ground state is inferred after days at 4.2 K using radiative cooling, a 149 s first-excited-state lifetime and a 5.4 meV gap. It is not directly state-resolved certification; spin populations need not be thermalized.

The molecular mass balance m_HD=m_p+m_d+m_e-E_ion(HD+)/c^2 uses the total positive ionization energy relative to free nuclei and electron. The predicted/direct comparison shares mass-reference and theoretical inputs; it is not independent-facility validation.

Reported mass values are conditional on the stated preparation, reference constants and correction model. Raw acquisition, original covariance and uncertainty propagation have not been independently reproduced.
These measurements and calculations do not establish nucleon formation, intrinsic stability or a universal carrier minimum. Historical constants are not present-day recommended values.

limitations: Fink/Myers uses a separate FSU 8.5 T, 4.2 K trap with two simultaneously stored ions, alternated between the center and a 2 mm cyclotron orbit. Storage is simultaneous; the reported frequency readout is sequential.

Of 83 runs on 27 H2+ ions, the final analysis uses 33 runs on seven ions. The eight-Gaussian vibrational histogram is not the final mass fit. The supplement needed to audit selection and maximum-likelihood details was not obtained.

Vibrational v=0 does not imply rotational N=0. Long-lived rotational excitation is modeled, not directly measured. A 300 K parent-gas distribution and cascade calculation are assumptions, with uncertain desorption populations.
The adopted rotational correction is 15.8(16.4) ppt. The trend -5.1(12.4) ppt is not a detection of heating. Table III total correction is 65.2(19.0) ppt; the 19.0 includes statistical uncertainty.

The published final ratio uncertainty components are (7) statistical, (7) instrumental, (16) rotational and (19) total. The raw statistical entry is 6.3 ppt; the original weighting is not independently reproduced.

Conversion from H2+ to m_d/m_p uses electron and molecular binding inputs. The cited Olivares-Pilon/Baye and Yan/Zhang/Li binding calculations remain unreviewed upstream sources here; Korobov HD+ theory is not substituted for them.
The absolute m_d=2.013553212586(76) u uses the Heiße 2019 proton mass. Independent ratio acquisition does not make this derived absolute mass independent of that proton input.
The paper also quotes m_n=1.00866491594(42) u with AME 2016 binding 0.00238816995(42) u. That input differs from the Rau recalibration and is not silently replaced.

limitations: The 2021 FSU experiment measures both ions simultaneously in coupled magnetron orbits. It is distinct from the 2020 alternation between a central ion and a 2 mm parked ion.

At 8.5 T the separation radius is 0.79-0.82 mm and the common-mode radius is below 0.03 mm. Orbits about 0.4 mm from the central gas beam improve collision survival; this is not an intrinsic molecular lifetime.

Cooling is alternating on the detector resonance, but PnP phase readout is simultaneous. Phase fits and the cited Thompson thesis equations convert trap-modified frequencies to the free ratio; those upstream equations and raw phases are not independently replayed.
Field-noise rejection is not total-uncertainty reduction. Thermal relativistic noise remains and the reported gain per mass-2 run is only slightly above a factor of two.

limitations: Three H2+ ions give eleven plateaus (2, 6 and 3). The final three conditional branch means use five ratios with unique level assignments within each branch, not eleven independently assigned ground-state measurements.

Assignments use theoretical level spacings, polarizability and E2 selection rules. The discarded high branch requires initial N>=7 and is rejected using a population prior, not direct state readout. Moss 1993, Korobov 2018 and the population/polarizability inputs remain unreviewed upstream.

The three uncorrected R00(5 ms) values are 0.9992316599712(21), 0.9992316599589(29) and 0.9992316599550(27). Relative branch probabilities are estimated between 1:0.012:0.058 and 1:0.13:0.27; the missing supplement prevents replay of those probabilities.

The published mass ratio assumes the most probable assignment. The other two branches lower it by 2.7 or 3.6 quoted standard uncertainties. These discrete alternatives are not included in the stated conditional Gaussian uncertainty and are not uniquely excluded.

limitations: The verifier uses printed branch centers and a shared 31.8e-12 correction, Korobov H2+ energy and rounded historical m_e, m_p and mass-energy conversion constants. It does not estimate state assignments or branch probabilities.

The proton quotient uses the printed direct deuteron mass and printed mass ratio. Its agreement with the rounded reported value verifies central arithmetic only; uncertainty propagation and independence are not established.
The lower branch shifts are measured in the published 9e-12 mass-ratio uncertainty. They remain discrete alternatives; the verifier does not average them or construct a new recommended uncertainty.

Table I corrections in absolute ratio units of 1e-12 are 29.5(1.4), 2.9(2.9), ion-ion <0.1, -1.1(0.2) and +0.5(0.5), with total 31.8(3.7). Naive independent quadrature of the listed nonzero errors gives about 3.265, not 3.7. Full covariance and rounding details are unavailable; no erroneous published uncertainty is established.
H2+ ground-state ionization energy is 131058.1219937(6) cm^-1 in Korobov 2017 Table V. It is distinct from the HD+ entry and from the older binding calculations cited in Fink 2020.

The NRQED calculation uses CODATA 2014 constants and spin-averaged energies. The quoted uncertainty is theoretical; the separate Rydberg and mass-ratio uncertainties are excluded. Wavefunctions, higher-order approximations and code are not replayed.
Use m_H2=2*m_p+m_e-E_ion(H2+)/c^2. Since both ions carry one positive charge, R=nu(H2+)/nu(D+)=m_d/m_H2. A reciprocal ratio or positive binding addition is a different equation.
Published inferences retain their preparation, calibration and model assumptions. Source reading and central arithmetic do not reproduce acquisition, covariance or propagated uncertainty.
These records do not establish nucleon formation, intrinsic particle stability or universal carrier minima. Publication-date constants are not automatically current recommendations.

records.definition: Mutual contributions to a specified joint outcome under declared conditions.
records.finding: A positive coupling coefficient does not prove bounded energy, stability or a necessary edge. Removing a required contribution and losing the target supports the necessity hypothesis; it is not its falsifier.

citations.locator: inactive-inequality

records.definition: A restriction on the admissible states, trajectories or operations of a specified model.
records.finding: An inequality is not generally an equality. A constrained optimum needs appropriate feasibility, multiplier and optimality conditions; tightening an inactive constraint need not change the outcome. For differentiable convex objectives/inequalities and affine equalities, the full KKT conditions are sufficient: primal feasibility, nonnegative inequality multipliers, complementary slackness and stationarity. With Slater regularity they are also necessary; arbitrary stationary points of a constrained Lagrangian are not automatically minima.
records.name: Constraint

records.definition: A closed influence path in a specified dynamical or intervention model.
records.finding: Feedback sign and gain magnitude are distinct. Stability needs the actual time domain, dynamics and delay assumptions. det(I-G)=0 is not a universal definition of criticality. For autonomous finite-dimensional linear x[n+1]=M*x[n], asymptotic stability requires all eigenvalues strictly inside the unit circle; boundary cases need additional analysis. For dx/dt=M*x, the corresponding condition is strictly negative real parts.
records.name: Feedback
