studies.finding: Early neuronal-appearing labels and later nonneuronal profiles coexist with an adult neuronal-detection null. Repeated doses, shared specimens and separate phenotype assays cannot establish a universal cessation or memory mechanism.
limitations: Eighteen rhesus monkeys span E140 to seventeen years: seventeen receive autoradiography and one E144 animal is used only for electron-microscopic GFAP. Table 1 contains four adult animals aged five, ten, ten and seventeen years at collection. Their seven, three, five and one injections total sixteen exposures, not sixteen independent animals.

Methods specifies six early developmental animals with one intravenous 5-10 mCi/kg tritiated-thymidine injection and one-hour survival. Table 1 instead prints one day for these rows. The eleven additional animals are described as surviving five weeks to two years, while Table 1 includes fourteen days, three years and six years. No adult one-hour cohort is documented; early developmental sampling cannot supply an adult short-interval null.

For adult cases 112883, 012980, 012376 and 021583, ages, injection counts and survival correspond to Rakic (1985) cases 12, 10, 11 and 8. This is evidence of overlapping material, pending original identity confirmation. Shared juvenile identifiers also have discordant age/survival reporting: 030783 is P149-P184 here versus seven months at death in 1985; 031683 is P507-P549 and six weeks here versus nineteen months and thirty-five days. Neither independent pooling nor silent record merging is justified.

Left hemispheres were sectioned at 8 micrometres and exposed for 10-18 weeks. Heavy light-microscopic labeling is more than half the maximum grain count in the most intensely labeled cells of each case. Electron microscopy uses four nuclear grains under low-background conditions. These distinct assay thresholds must not be merged with each other or with the 1985 threshold.

GFAP immunochemistry uses 30-micrometre vibratome sections from five animals. Antibody penetration reaches only about three micrometres. The normal-goat-serum primary-antibody control is incubated at 4 degrees C, whereas primary antiserum incubation is at room temperature. A negative GFAP profile need not be a neuron; technical false negatives and other glial or precursor identities remain possible.

Postnatal short-interval and longer-survival groups contain different animals. Approximately 150 sections across three longer-survival ages yielded eight profiles classified morphologically as definitive granule neurons, only one in P90-P155. These are sampled profiles, not eight animals, a clonal lineage or a daily birth rate; Nissl morphology has acknowledged identity limits.

The P149-P184 interval is thirty-five days/five weeks in Table 1 and text, but Figure 4B says six weeks. Figure 5 uses P507-P549. Neither is an adult cohort. The five-year-old seven-injection animal has about two labeled profiles per ten sections at three months, all small SGZ profiles without typical neuronal morphology. The seventeen-year-old animal retains a label given six years earlier; collection age does not date a new division at seventeen.

GFAP composition in Figures 7-10 concerns small SGZ cells without birth-label selection. The E144 animal was never thymidine-labeled; about half its sampled small cells are GFAP-positive. Approximately 75% at six months and a majority at later ages do not quantify the astrocytic fraction of adult newborn cells or prove two founder lineages.

The combined electron-microscopic assay examined 120 ultrathin semiserial sections from selected areas in each of three animals aged six months, one and a half years, and five years. A dozen reliably radiolabeled cells were found, six GFAP-positive. This is a pooled three-age subset, not twelve adult neurons or a representative adult astrocyte fraction. Figure 11 is juvenile; Figure 12 is the five-year-old animal.

Figure 12B is described as an oligodendroglial type in Results but as resting microglia in the caption. Its specific subtype remains unresolved. No labeled profile had reported neuronal ultrastructure or synapses in the examined sections; this sampling-limited null does not prove absence of all neuronal precursor potential.

The discussion calls sixteen injections to four adult animals equivalent to independent labeling experiments. Repeated exposures share animals and cumulative label windows. The eleven-of-twelve-month coverage is also pooled across animals and ages, not a matched adult seasonal experiment. No formal rare-neuron detection bound or exact cessation age is calculated.

No lineage tracing identifies whether phenotypes arise from separate committed founders or a common multipotent founder. The discussion allows other glial lines, undifferentiated cells and potential neuronal differentiation under other conditions. Regional co-occurrence and GFAP phenotype cannot close a precursor-to-neuron construction rule.

Gliogenesis, replacement and stable-neuron memory roles are interpretations. No paired birth/death census identifies population feedback, and no functional or behavioral test establishes that neuron turnover impairs memory. The adult autoradiographic null remains distinct from a universal prohibition on adult neurogenesis.

All nineteen article pages, Materials and Methods, Table 1 and Figures 1-12 were read in the Europe PMC PDF; the table and all twelve figures were visually inspected. Original animal and section records, raw microscopy and quantitative analysis were not obtained or independently reproduced.

studies.finding: PV activation suppresses population cycle markers and PV inhibition increases them; tested SST/VIP manipulations retain nulls. Conditional gamma2 deletion changes early activation and later clone composition. Isolation retains an EdU difference under PV activation, while MCM2 housing contrasts are nonsignificant. Full feedback closure and exclusive mediation remain unresolved.
limitations: Adult mouse preparations use nestin-GFP, PV/SST/VIP-Cre and nestin-CreERT2;Z/EG lines with gamma2-floxed or control alleles. Sex and a complete group-specific animal manifest are not reported. Tamoxifen is a single 62 mg/kg intraperitoneal dose at 6-10 weeks. The Methods require at least four weeks after AAV surgery; schematic week labels do not supply exact ages for every animal.

Acute 300-micrometre slices were recorded at 32-34 degrees C, with RGL voltage clamp at -65 mV and 5 mM kynurenic acid. The internal solution is ambiguously printed as 135 mM CsCl gluconate. Clamp-current sign does not directly identify native membrane polarization, spiking or cell-cycle entry.

Main text, Online Methods and Supplementary Figure 1 print 200 mM for focal GABA/muscimol application; no micromolar substitution is made. Etomidate is 100 nM in the main text/Figure 1 but 10 micromolar in Methods. The etomidate dose remains unresolved, and pharmacological sensitivity does not establish receptor stoichiometry.

Population experiments use five consecutive days of stimulation, eight hours per day: ChR2 blue light at 472 nm, 5-ms pulses at 8 Hz for 30 seconds every five minutes, or continuous 593-nm eNpHR light. AAV volume, delivered light power and a full opsin-negative illumination control are not reported. No-light sham comparisons include the effects of the complete light protocol.

On day five, EdU is injected intraperitoneally at 41.1 mg/kg six times, two hours apart, with collection two hours after the last injection. Repeated injections are not independent replicates. EdU incorporation and MCM2 expression are cycle-related endpoints, not counts of completed neuronal differentiation, integrated neurons or an instantaneous birth rate.

Population scoring uses 40-micrometre sections, every sixth section, and nestin-positive inverted-Y morphology over an EdU- or MCM2-positive nucleus. Optogenetic counts are limited to one millimetre anterior and posterior to the injection. Densities per cubic millimetre and the MCM2-positive fraction have distinct denominators. Analyses are described as blinded; random assignment, raw unit records and multiplicity-adjusted tests are not supplied.

At two and seven days after induction, one GFP-positive RGL is classified as a quiescent clone and two or more nuclei as an activated clone. These are fixed-tissue, spatially assigned clones using a referenced method, not live observations of every division or independently verified common ancestry. Supplementary Figure 2d plots one dentate gyrus per dot; hemispheres and clones cannot automatically be treated as independent animals.

Gamma2 immunostaining is shown in RGLs, but Supplementary Figure 2f electrophysiology tests GFP-positive neurons at thirty days, not RGLs. Its seven-of-ten cKO response pattern is not a measured RGL deletion efficiency. Recombination can persist in descendants, so later survival or differentiation may contribute to clone composition.

Thirty-day Figure 3f and Supplementary Figure 3e use incompletely reconciled clone denominators: the supplementary pie categories omit single-R and no-R classes. N includes intermediate progenitors or neurons, not exclusively mature neurons. Exact class percentages must not be pooled or converted to transition probabilities.

The population diazepam protocol is 5 mg/kg intraperitoneally once daily for five days. The clonal drug comparison instead uses six daily doses after tamoxifen and analysis at seven days. Diazepam is systemic. Pairwise drug responses or nulls without a reported genotype-by-drug interaction do not isolate an exclusive cell-autonomous mediator.

Social isolation starts immediately after weaning and lasts at least six weeks before labeling. The two housing conditions are crossed with light versus sham; this is not a selective learning manipulation. PV activity and extracellular GABA are not measured as the intervening response to isolation in the same animals.

Figure 5c retains higher EdU-positive RGL density in isolated versus group-housed animals under PV light stimulation (reported P < 0.05). In that same housing comparison, MCM2-positive density and fraction are nonsignificant (P > 0.1). These endpoints do not support complete abolition of the isolation effect or equivalence; the light-treated group is also distinct from the untreated group-housed baseline.

Figure 4 population comparisons use three or four animals per condition; Figure 5c uses four. Reported Student t-tests do not provide an equivalence margin, complete unit manifest or a formal factorial interaction. SST/VIP nulls apply to the tested lines, protocols and readouts, not all possible interneuron functions.

No matched experiment follows physiological circuit demand through PV signaling, RGL division, newborn-neuron survival and functional integration to restoration of circuit output. Supplementary Figure 8 imports schematic connectivity proportions, not measured weights. A reported reconstruction covering over 200 RGLs is spatial coverage, not 200 verified functional contacts or a minimum carrier count. Movie legends were read; movie files and custom reconstruction code were not replayed.

All six main PDF pages, Figures 1-5, Online Methods and all nine supplementary PDF pages with Figures 1-8 and Movie 1-3 legends were reviewed. Raw animal-level data, microscopy, recordings, movie files and analysis code were not obtained or independently reproduced.

studies.finding: Sox2-labeled populations show expandable culture potential and neuronal, astroglial or Sox2-retaining phenotypes in distinct assays. Sparse mixed clusters support conditional common-founder and self-renewal interpretations. Running comparisons report increased cycle-related markers and nonsignificant GFP-density differences, but reporter-control identity is unresolved. Complete lineage cycles and population-maintenance mechanisms remain hypotheses.
limitations: The 5.5-kb Sox2-promoter GFP transgenic line 1F7 is distinct from the 3.1-kb Sox2-GFP/Cre viral cassette and ROSA26 GFP or beta-gal reporters. Initial histology uses six-week mice; supplementary IHC specifies six to nine weeks, whereas clonal tracing uses six-week to three-month ROSA26 mice. Sex and a complete assay-specific animal manifest are not reported.

Marker meaning depends on niche and morphology. SGZ radial processes express nestin, GFAP and BLBP; lack of somatic signal makes nonradial nestin/GFAP assessment infeasible, not a demonstrated negative phenotype. Hilar astrocytic and SVZ ependymal marker combinations cannot be assigned the SGZ stem-cell interpretation automatically.

FGF2/EGF growth conditions and FACS select an expandable culture population. The preparation pools four pairs of hippocampi; the complete independent culture/animal allocation is unavailable. Enrichment and serial passage do not measure in vivo self-renewal frequency or establish that every cultured cell preserves its original in vivo potential.

The seven-day 5-micromolar forskolin assay shows neuronal and astrocytic markers. RIP-positive oligodendroglial differentiation uses a separate coculture with P0 rat hippocampal neurons and a donor beta-gal label. These conditions do not show in vivo tripotency, functional myelination or all three fates and serial renewal in one fully documented founder lineage.

At seven days, the lentiviral control reports SOX2 in 70% of GFP-positive cells and NeuN-positive off-target labeling of 26 +/- 3%, with n=800 cells, not 800 animals. BrdU selection is used to exclude nondividing off-target neurons. Animal-level denominators, initial recombination timing and complete lineage specificity are not established by this endpoint control.

Population fate mapping uses 100 mg/kg BrdU daily for seven days, starting ten or twenty-eight days after lentivirus. Methods specifies collection four weeks after the last injection, while Figure 3A marks analyses at days thirty-eight and fifty-eight. These statements do not reconcile to one exact label-age schedule; the injection route is unspecified.

Table 1 uses separate immunostaining panels, so marker percentages are not a partition of one cohort. Its S-100beta row prints three positive cells among thirty-two and 6.1%; these disagree because 3/32 is 9.375%. Neither value is silently substituted, and exact pooled fate probabilities are not admitted.

Retroviral specificity is reported as 92 +/- 1.7% SOX2 colabeling at seven days in a separate n=3 control. Twenty-one-day lineage assignments rely on sparse labeling and proximity, without founder barcodes, live division trees or a reported chance-collision bound. Clusters and hemispheres are nested within twenty-seven animals.

Table 2 lists 301 neuron-only, seven astrocyte-only, ten Sox2-only, fifteen Sox2-plus-neuron, one neuron-plus-astrocyte and twenty-nine undetermined clusters, totaling 363 across fifty-four hemispheres. Homogeneous categories include one- and two-cell clusters. These are cluster counts, not independent animal counts or an unbiased lineage-fate probability distribution.

Figure S4 traverses optical depth in micrometres, not elapsed time. The radial-process example is a fixed mixed cluster, not observation of its founder or a conversion event. Figure 4D has differing GFP and beta-gal panel labels; reporter identity needs clarification before panel-specific quantitative reuse.

Running Methods specifies seven transgenic runners and seven wild-type littermate controls, but Figure 5 shows and counts GFP-positive cells in both groups. The main paper and supplement do not resolve this control-genotype conflict. A matched reporter-genotype intervention effect is therefore not admitted.

The comparison uses individual cages with or without wheel access, seven daily 100 mg/kg BrdU injections and collection twenty-four hours after the last injection; the route is unreported. Figure 5A and caption do not uniquely fix wheel-access duration. Accumulated BrdU, terminal Ki67 and DCX are different readouts, not completed neuron production or functional integration.

Figure 5 reports densities per million cubic micrometres. GFP is sampled across the dentate rostrocaudal axis, while other markers use four dorsal hippocampal sections. Supplementary histology uses forty-micrometre sections; the stated every-twelfth-section and 440-micrometre interval lack a spacing-reference convention. GFP counting is described as blind; full animal allocation, raw measurements and multiplicity-adjusted analyses are unavailable.

Reported GFP-density comparisons have P=0.1724, n=7 for total reporter cells and P=0.1125, n=5 for radial cells. These nonsignificant comparisons do not establish equivalence, conservation of whole-population counts or a constant pool through time. The control-genotype conflict also applies to these nulls.

Figure 6 models population maintenance and possible radial/nonradial lineage relations. Its caption explicitly distinguishes asymmetric contribution at population level from asymmetric division of individual cells. Birth, death, survival, marker kinetics and a regulated feedback variable are not jointly measured; no universal stem-cell minimum or closed homeostatic construction is established.

All main scientific text, methods, six figures, two tables and the complete fourteen-page supplement were reviewed. Raw images, animal-level records and custom analysis code were not independently reproduced.

studies.finding: PF sample selectivity can reappear between distractors, while match enhancement and repetition suppression have different task dependence. These observations do not establish a causal local storage or PF-to-IT route.
limitations: Two rhesus monkeys supplied 264 screened PF units; 145 task-responsive units were retained (98 in the ABBA-trained animal and 47 in the standard-task animal). The other 109 units were not studied further. Cells are nested within two animals; this is not an unbiased PF prevalence estimate. Sex and ages are unspecified.

The sample and test images last 500 ms with 1000-ms blank intervals and zero to four intervening nonmatches. ABBA trials repeat an irrelevant nonmatch; standard trials do not. Task/training differences are confounded with animal identity. PF visual responses use 90-290 ms after onset and delay activity the last 600 ms of each blank interval.

The text reports forty delay-selective units, including 33/98 ABBA and 7/47 standard units; Table 1 instead lists 32/98 for ABBA. Match-enhancement counts also differ across the text and table, with mixed response types. No exact reconciled subgroup prevalence or exclusive partition is admitted.

The 135 IT units were previously recorded in the ABBA animal and reanalyzed. They are not simultaneous paired PF-IT recordings or an independent replication. Figure 7 pools forty PF units across two animals against twenty-five IT units from one animal; selection and animal composition differ.

Best/worst-sample traces use selected neurons and sample rankings. Reported half-trial discriminant classification excludes the first delay and averages 20.8% versus six-way chance of 16.7%; the paper does not specify that unit selection was nested within training folds. No classification, multiplicity correction or neural minimum is independently reproduced.

PF feedback to IT is proposed in the Discussion. The authors explicitly state that the direct PF-deactivation test of IT match enhancement had not been tried. Response precedence, delay persistence and ramping do not identify an exclusive local recurrence, directed feedback route, accumulator or complete control circuit.

QED_L removes spatial photon zero modes on every time slice. QED_TL removes only the four-momentum zero mode and has an ill-defined T-to-infinity limit at fixed L for the conventional charged-particle mass extraction. This is a regulator distinction, not two experimental forces.

At order alpha, the leading mass correction is -q^2*alpha*kappa/(2*L)*(1+2/(m*L)), with kappa approximately 2.837297 in units hbar=c=1. Universality through 1/L^2 assumes the photon is the only massless asymptotic state and the charged particle is stable and nondegenerate with states sharing its quantum numbers.

Terms of order 1/L^3 can depend on internal structure and spin; a point-fermion coefficient cannot be imposed on every hadron. Vanishing leading q^2 terms for a neutral particle do not prove absence of all finite-volume effects.

In the full QCD+QED theory the paper's continuum prescription retains an extremely small nonzero cutoff because of QED triviality. Its practical extrapolation does not establish a nonperturbative interacting QED limit at exactly zero lattice spacing.

The paper reports a 5e-10 relative uncertainty contribution from recoil constants, negligible at its measurement precision. This does not make recoil itself negligible or set omitted kinematic effects identically to zero.

The 1999 inverse-meter conversions are 1.331025045(11)e-15 u and 1.239841870(54)e-6 eV per inverse meter. The first is a mass-equivalent conversion h/(m_u*c), the second is hc/e; energy and mass units are not interchangeable without c^2.

The later author report uses d220(ILL2.5)=1.920155822(96)e-10 m, retaining a 5e-8 relative uncertainty after enlarging the underlying adjustment uncertainty. Its deuterium row reuses Kessler data and is not a new capture experiment.

The 2005 author report notes that erroneous 2004 lattice measurements affected the 2002 adjustment, and uses the 1998 adjustment for this recalculation. Those upstream measurements and their erratum have not been independently reviewed here.

comparisons.alternative: The unequal-voltage PNP nondoublet measurement is unbiased at the same precision.
assumptions: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

The SOF signal is a classical cyclotron amplitude produced by two separated pulses, not a quantum-state amplitude or an entanglement measurement. Figure 1 uses evolution times up to 50 s for the precision estimate.

Figure 2 compares an N+ ion at approximately 5 V with the same species at 10 V and an N2+ ion at 10 V, with a 22.5 mV axial offset. The approximately 3 ppb unequal-voltage shift disappears at the reported precision with the common-voltage procedure.

Table I bounds residual magnetic, electrostatic and relativistic systematic terms at approximately 0.030, 0.025 and 0.020 ppb for the specified N+/N2+ settings. These are configuration-specific error estimates, not zero corrections or universal bounds.

The first two Table II(a) reference ratios depend on electron mass and binding energies. Their agreement near 0.15 ppb tests those controls; it does not prove absence of every systematic effect in all other ion comparisons.
The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

For the same magnetic field, omega_2/omega_1=(m_1/abs(q_1))/(m_2/abs(q_2)). Equal charges permit a mass ratio; the Ar+/Ar++ entry requires the charge factor and is not a literal ratio of almost equal ionic masses.
The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

Heiße 2017 prints m_C=11.9967096264139(10) u and 0.08 ppt relative uncertainty. Heiße 2019 prints 11.99670962641385(8) u but still states 0.08 ppt; the printed (8) corresponds to about 0.00667 ppt. This unresolved uncertainty discrepancy is not silently repaired.

The proton-electron ratio in Heiße 2019 assumes zero covariance because the dominant proton and electron systematic uncertainties differ. That assumption is not proof of complete statistical independence.

The stored ions are measured alternately under the same trap voltages, using separate axial resonators. Randomized species order reduces linear drift; it does not make sequential measurements simultaneous or statistically independent.
The proton dataset comprises thirteen runs and three ion pairs, with about 300 hours of acquisition over two months. Runs, cycles, ion pairs and publications are not independent replications.
The planar fit extrapolates the deliberately excited cyclotron motion to zero using R_i=R_stat+a*S_p^2+b*S_C^2. Thermal axial and cyclotron motion still requires systematic corrections.
The 2019 reanalysis corrects the estimated ion temperatures and a minor measurement-program flaw in the 2017 datasets. The two publications cannot be averaged as independent proton-mass experiments.

Heiße 2017 Figure 3 lists phase-unwrapping times 0.1, 1, 2 and 5 s; Heiße 2019 describes 0.5, 1, 2 and 5 s. The four final 10 s phase evolutions are distinct from those unwrapping stages; the differing descriptions are retained.

The 2017 abbreviation MT denotes the measurement trap; in 2019 PT denotes the precision trap and MT the magnetometer trap. The proposed simultaneous three-ion readout and magnetic shim coils were not used in the reported proton campaign.

The proton campaign had C4=(0 +/- 6.3)e-6 and C6=(-6.8 +/- 0.4)e-4. The improved Table VI tuning and proposed millikelvin cooling describe other conditions, not the acquisition used for the reported mass.

Review modern hydrogen precision measurements and complete radiative contributions before extending the approximate 1947 Lamb/Bethe comparison.

Recover Lee acquisition, selection and effective-exposure/confidence construction before independently certifying the reported abundance limit. Review independent materials and charge searches without pooling unmatched preparations.

Recover the Dürr configurations, correlators, covariance, fit-quality weighting and fitting implementation for independent spectrum replay. Extend the isospin-symmetric calculation with reviewed electromagnetic/isospin-breaking evidence before representing a proton-neutron mass difference.

The remaining fits infer masses and couplings across the simulated volumes and masses; their width sensitivity is limited and errors are large. Multiple levels and cross-correlators for precise widths are outside this paper.

limitations: PNP detects the ion after coherent radial-to-axial transfer. Its resonant voltages differ for N+ and N2+, changing equilibrium position in stray fields. The SOF protocol keeps the evolution voltage common and changes it only for detection.

The SOF signal is a classical cyclotron amplitude produced by two separated pulses, not a quantum-state amplitude or an entanglement measurement. Figure 1 uses evolution times up to 50 s for the precision estimate.

Figure 2 compares an N+ ion at approximately 5 V with the same species at 10 V and an N2+ ion at 10 V, with a 22.5 mV axial offset. The approximately 3 ppb unequal-voltage shift disappears at the reported precision with the common-voltage procedure.

Table I bounds residual magnetic, electrostatic and relativistic systematic terms at approximately 0.030, 0.025 and 0.020 ppb for the specified N+/N2+ settings. These are configuration-specific error estimates, not zero corrections or universal bounds.

The first two Table II(a) reference ratios depend on electron mass and binding energies. Their agreement near 0.15 ppb tests those controls; it does not prove absence of every systematic effect in all other ion comparisons.
The measured ion has three trap modes. The free cyclotron frequency is reconstructed from their squared frequencies; the trap cyclotron mode alone is not the free frequency.
The paper writes omega_c=q*B/(m*c) in Gaussian units. In SI the expression is omega_c=abs(q)*B/m for the frequency magnitude; an angular frequency differs from cycles per second by 2*pi.

For the same magnetic field, omega_2/omega_1=(m_1/abs(q_1))/(m_2/abs(q_2)). Equal charges permit a mass ratio; the Ar+/Ar++ entry requires the charge factor and is not a literal ratio of almost equal ionic masses.
The ions are loaded and measured alternately, not simultaneously. Removing a fitted magnetic drift does not make all residuals or adjacent ratios statistically independent.
These are reported measurements and conditional inferences. Raw phase records, drift fits, chemical-energy inputs and complete covariance have not been independently replayed.

A charged-ion frequency, neutral-atom mass and inferred neutron mass are different quantities. These results do not establish nucleon formation, lifetime, stability or a universal constituent minimum.

The 1993 and 1994 publications belong to the same MIT measurement program. Disjoint acquisition and cross-publication covariance are not established; the two papers cannot be treated as independent replications or averaged as independent results.

limitations: The 1994 result is a global least-squares solution of twenty pairwise comparisons. Its covariance matrix determines uncertainties of correlated atomic masses and mass differences; the short article does not provide that matrix or every input ratio.
For a mass difference, Var(D-H)=Var(D)+Var(H)-2*Cov(D,H). Adding printed marginal errors in quadrature assumes zero covariance and is not a reconstruction of the published fit.

The authors report reduced chi-square 0.74 and redundant routes to the mass table. These internal checks constrain the stated error model; they do not logically exclude every possible common systematic.

The quoted 2.6e-10 relative rms magnetic fluctuation applies to a single frequency measurement in the 1994 analysis. A typical one-night ratio error near 1e-10 and the final fitted mass uncertainties have different averaging domains.

The 1993 treatment describes approximately Gaussian residuals for its example; the 1994 robust estimator downweights non-Gaussian outliers. These are different analysis descriptions, not interchangeable procedures.
The carbon-12 neutral-atom reference has mass exactly 12 u by definition. A carbon ion differs by electron mass and ionization energy; treating C+ as exactly 12 u is incorrect.

Converting molecular-ion comparisons to neutral isolated ground-state atoms requires electron, chemical-binding and ionization-energy terms. The 1994 analysis uses ideal-gas heats of formation at 0 K; this is not the trap temperature.
A neutral hydrogen atom is not a bare proton and a neutral deuterium atom is not a deuteron. Nuclear masses require removal of electronic contributions.
Table II(b) of the 1993 paper expresses masses in nu (1e-9 u). Its H and D values become 1.0078250317(7) u and 2.0141017779(6) u; the 1994 H value is 1.0078250316(5) u.

Subtracting the printed 1994 D and H central values gives 1.0062767463 u. Kessler adopts the dimensionless relative-mass difference 1.00627674630(71); its 0.71e-9 uncertainty is not independently recovered from the missing mass-fit covariance.

The 1994 neutron value 1.0086649235(23) u already uses the Greene1986 deuteron binding energy. The 1993 neutron value uses the Wapstra1990 binding-energy compilation. Neither is a direct measurement of a neutral neutron in the trap.

The upstream H/D mass information is an input to the capture-based neutron inference. Feeding a neutron mass already derived from capture binding energy back as an independent confirmation would conceal a shared input.
The 1993/1994 mass inputs are historical values. They are not current recommended constants, a new SI kilogram definition or independently traced inputs to the Borsanyi calculation.

limitations: Schuh uses 120 cycles over 23 days, with 73 cycles at 40 s and the others at 20 s, and approximately 140 minutes per full cycle. Two 4.6 ms magnetron pulses and an intentionally deformed readout potential distinguish this experiment from proton-mass PnA acquisition.

The readout uses C2=-0.5997, C4=-0.00223(18), C6=0.014(4) and a maximal magnetron radius near 274 micrometers. Harmonic potential during phase evolution and deformed potential during readout must not be conflated.

The 43 microhertz statistical error is enlarged by sqrt(2) to 61 microhertz because the reduced chi-square is 2. Tilt fluctuations cannot be separated from voltage fluctuations by the axial signal alone.

The image-charge difference subtracts ideal 390.723(1) mHz, magnetic 0.056(21) mHz and tilt/ellipticity 0.188(37) mHz from 393.258(61)(77) mHz. The resulting 2.291(61)(111) mHz combines correlated correction uncertainties.

The 73 and 37 microhertz tilt contributions are correlated and add to 110 microhertz. The two 21 microhertz magnetic contributions cancel in the stated analysis; quadrature of all marginal errors would misrepresent that covariance.

Appendix A uses the 2017 proton mass and compares an axial calibration ratio over 1000 measurements drawn from both the image-charge and proton campaigns. This shared input prevents a claim of fully independent proton-mass validation.

The page 6 prose labels a ratio of magnetron frequencies as axial; Appendix A explicitly defines the required ratio using nu_z. The calibration follows the axial observable and retains the printed discrepancy.

Schuh Table I gives an experimental image-charge magnetron difference 2.291(126) mHz and a simulated difference 2.377(21) mHz. Table II separately prints an experimental free-cyclotron correction 471.9(23.9) microhertz per charge state and a full-geometry value 475.4(2.1)(3.6).

Dividing the Table I difference by the charge-state difference of five gives 458.2 microhertz, before the small axial contribution, rather than Table II 471.9. The conversion between these printed entries has not been recovered. Both tables are preserved; neither is silently rewritten or claimed to be an exact replay of the other.

boundary.summary: The graph separates definitions, scoped observations, computational results, experimental interventions and hypotheses. Each scientific claim records the passages read, the preparation and the limits of its evidence. Behavioral success and fitted models do not identify a unique neural mechanism; mathematical specifications do not establish physical instances or universal minima. Levels organize the display. Review of the source catalogue and cross-domain dependencies remains incomplete.

routingPolicy.acceptance: Eight complete contexts, three aggregate functional relations, six exact spreadsheet rows, all four route candidates adjudicated in each context, negative contract tests and reproducible current output.
evidenceRules: Every context is a complete comparison protocol: its baseline and intervention arms must be read jointly. A context ID is not an individual treatment state or animal identity.
Bind each operating relation to complete experimental context IDs in addition to publication IDs. A publication containing several species is not one compatible preparation.

Represent each supported bridge as an aggregate light-drive-to-output functional relation. Candidate route decompositions are explanatory records, not separately measured synapses or physical construction rules.
Primary, secondary and tertiary routes are candidates; the non-primary candidate is an inclusive OR of secondary and tertiary. Supporting this disjunction does not identify either component.
Pharmacological and constitutive genetic contrasts have their declared specificity limits. Neither is represented as a perfect graph-edge deletion.
Keep mean background and flash intensity distinct despite their shared R*/rod/s unit; preserve nominal prose values separately from spreadsheet coordinates.
Replay published Figure 6F summary ratios without inventing sample-level data, standard errors, causal weights or carrier-count thresholds.
Existing publication-only fragments cannot participate in a context-qualified path. For a path, require a single complete context shared by every relation; pairwise overlap is insufficient.

Each case declares which route candidates the selected contrast can identify; unsupported disjunction-to-member promotion is rejected. These bounds are retrospective curation decisions, not an automatic biological identification theorem.

Unknown parameters remain explicit null values with named limitations, never wildcards or borrowed values from a nearby experiment. Complete context records do not imply a fully specified replication protocol.
routingPolicy.exposure: The existing retinal pilot, Grimes 2018 and Jin 2022 abstracts, selected Results/Methods and the Grimes Figure 6 workbook were inspected before this policy. This is an internal retrospective reconstruction, not a preregistered or held-out test.
limits: No complete toad-to-primate or cross-publication cascade is admitted.
No developmental generation, exhaustive minimality, independent prediction, geometric advantage or physical CRT promotion is established.
routingPolicy.scope: Compare specified OFF retinal-output routing experiments. Do not pool species, RGC classes, genotype contrasts, stimulus protocols or adaptation histories.

scope.levelInterpretation: Display groups inherited from the catalogue; no universal hierarchy, developmental order or derivation from Level 0 is inferred.
scope.summary: Partial source reconstruction of Level-0 definitions and scoped physical, optical, retinal, visual and neural records. Formal specifications, computational models, experimental preparations, reported observations and conditional interpretations have distinct meanings and evidence. Reviewed studies retain their own systems, selections, observables, uncertainty limits and unresolved contradictions. Physical records distinguish quantum-field definitions, scattering and decay measurements, Bell tests, vacuum quantities, QCD running, lattice spectra and charge searches. Calibrated masses, detector unloading times, storage-loss rates and intrinsic-lifetime interpretations are separate quantities. Neutron survival studies retain production years, diagnostic controls, shared data and non-decay-loss corrections. Four-flavor QCD+QED mass splittings retain physical-point inputs, finite-volume prescriptions, convention-dependent components and the additional experimental input to a calibrated ratio. Capture-based neutron-mass inference distinguishes campaign angles, crystal calibration, nuclear recoil, unit conversions, adopted isotope masses and recalibration of shared data. Penning-trap inputs distinguish charge-normalized frequency ratios, voltage controls, neutral-atom corrections and correlated mass fits. LIONTRAP separates original acquisition, experimental reanalysis, shared-data controls and conditional electrode-geometry predictions. Cross-domain construction, universal carrier minima, downward causal rules and a derivation of quantum theory from Level 0 remain unestablished. No whole-graph scientific validation is claimed.

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for the author's proposed prephysical foundation.
vocabulary.finding: A hypothesis vocabulary, not an established physical stage; the conditional Level-0 rules and unsuccessful objecthood case state the actual evidence boundary.
vocabulary.name: Proto Field

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for quantum descriptions and examples.
vocabulary.finding: Display placement is not a unique scale, a temporal stage or proof that quantum systems arise from the proposed foundation.
vocabulary.name: Quantum

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for atomic and related material examples.
vocabulary.finding: Domains overlap; the number 2 does not establish derivation depth or a universal transition from every quantum description.
vocabulary.name: Atomic

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for biochemical examples.
vocabulary.finding: Biochemical organization requires mechanism-specific review, not inference from its position after atoms.
vocabulary.name: Biochemical

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for cellular examples.
vocabulary.finding: A cellular display group does not establish autonomous objecthood or a universal four-phase construction rule.
vocabulary.name: Cellular

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for multicellular structures and functions.
vocabulary.finding: Functions, organs, regulation and organism formation require separate relations; grouping them does not make their carriers interchangeable.
vocabulary.name: Multicellular

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for behavior and cognition examples.
vocabulary.finding: Behavioral description does not prove a new physical law or a unique complexity rank.
vocabulary.name: Behavioral

vocabulary.definition: A historical display group for social organization examples.
vocabulary.finding: Social group placement does not identify a formation mechanism, minimal population or distinct physical stratum.
vocabulary.name: Social

vocabulary.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for technological examples.

vocabulary.name: Technological

vocabulary.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for planetary examples.
vocabulary.finding: No level-9 source catalogue exists. Planetary scale does not imply greater complexity or later origin than society.
vocabulary.name: Planetary

vocabulary.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for civilizational examples.
vocabulary.finding: No level-10 source catalogue exists. This rubric overlaps social and technological descriptions and is not a validated physical layer.
vocabulary.name: Civilizational

vocabulary.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for spacefaring infrastructure examples.
vocabulary.finding: No level-11 source catalogue exists. Specified engineering systems would need their own evidence and admission decisions.
vocabulary.name: Spacefaring infrastructure

vocabulary.definition: A dictionary-only proposal for cosmic examples.
vocabulary.finding: No level-12 source catalogue exists. Cosmic chronology cannot be inferred from placement after society or infrastructure; mechanism narratives remain unreviewed.
vocabulary.name: Cosmic

vocabulary.definition: A dictionary-only speculative placeholder.
